item.title: Four Ways To Hold The Room
item.description: This week is four records that keep the low end open. One moves like sound-system dub, one brings Bristol pressure, one turns dubstep into industrial fog, and one bends toward warped techno. Different corners, same rule:…

item.title: One Dubplate, No Filler
item.description: Some weeks bring a full stack. This one brought a single record worth keeping close.

item.title: Weight Travels Well
item.description: The interesting records this week all do the same thing from different directions: they carry low-end across a border without dropping it.

item.title: Back On Air
item.description: This week moves from reconstructed live recordings to dubplate logic, deep jungle, and stripped halftime. It is a hard reset across several tempos, held together by low-end pressure.

item.title: Eleven Across the Low End
item.description: Astronomic — "Water falls" opens the deep-140 side with the sub in front and plenty of room around it. TIME WZRD — "Me N You" and SL33PY — "TUG" stay in that restrained pocket, where negative space carries as much force …

item.title: The Clock Comes Apart
item.description: Four records this week, and not one of them keeps time straight. They stretch it, fold it, drop it to half and let the tail ring out. The grid was a suggestion. What held instead was weight.

item.title: Convoys, Dubplates, and the Long Way Around
item.description: The low end took the scenic route this week. Nothing here came down the New York–London–Berlin line. The pressure arrived from a taxi rank in Durban, a dubplate cut in twenty copies, an imprint built around silence, and …

item.title: Three From the Deep End
item.description: Three records hold the center this week: self-released, dubwise, and patient enough to let the room do some of the work. None of them need to shout to sound enormous.
